speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
text: asked the Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (a) what are some community support mechanisms available to help individuals process the impact of international conflicts; and (b) how are global conflicts abroad being unpacked domestically to maintain social harmony and cohesion in Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our approach has been to foster better understanding of these developments and to explain the implications for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government strives to make such information available in a timely manner, including through Statements to this House.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is also important to provide space for civil dialogue on these issues and to allow Singaporeans to contribute in constructive ways.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This can deepen mutual understanding between communities and promote social cohesion.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation (RLAF), established by the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura or MUIS), provides channels for all Singaporeans to help.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I have two supplementary questions, one in English.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: One clarification to ask is, is this service that the Acting Minister has mentioned also available to communities beyond the Malay/Muslim community, given that it cuts across different groups?

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: And in Malay, please, Speaker. :   Mr Speaker and Acting Minister, the whole of Singapore remains concerned, as mentioned, with many feeling confused, worried and also troubled by this multi-faceted Middle East conflict.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: My first question – what are the Government's observations on the impact of this Middle East conflict so far, particularly on our Malay and Muslim communities, whether emotionally, spiritually or mentally?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, they have been very supportive all these years and I am thankful to all the asatizah for playing this role.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is where we see our asatizah go down to the ground.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They really roll up their sleeves and also try to share perspectives from what they know and how we can journey through together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And I am happy to share that they are very well aware and really plugged into the context of Singapore, as well as having a deep understanding of Islamic principles and what we ought to do in our lives as Muslims.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And also, with this in mind, they are also connected to the multiracial setting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Many of them are in settings like the Harmony Circles or even in some of the aspects of how we build our community together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If any fellow Singaporeans or any community leaders need their support, we welcome you to seek some guidance and opinion from the asatizah in the Asatizah Solace Care.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With regard to the second supplementary question, let me answer in Malay. :   We do not see every issue in isolation, but we look at them holistically in terms of how we can continue our country's development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We understand that this conflict can bring about a profound impact.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are conflicts that do not affect us as severely and there are others that are more complex for us to handle as a society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we do not take lightly the impact of any conflict on our country, our people, including the minority groups, even though they may not experience the impact or receive more detailed insights in this aspect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: How can we provide support to those who are affected as well as community organisations, including IMOs, MMOs and also our asatizah or religious teachers?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I mentioned, we have a multi-level approach.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also have approaches like conducting dialogues at various levels.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Some are conducted in safe spaces and others are organised with community organisations and their members.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If the issue is more complex and requires a more customised approach, we will also design it as such, where we see each issue as important and how we as a society can address it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But I am also heartened to see the maturity in the thinking and the stance of Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They prioritise national interest when dealing with these issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the grassroots level, we also have Harmony Circles, where our religious teachers and other community or religious organisations come together to discuss relevant issues, including the ongoing conflict, and think about how we can prioritise harmony and our life as a cohesive society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Therefore, this is the journey that we have charted over past decades until today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will continue to improve it and develop relevant networks and approaches, because we can see that the world today has changed and we need support from all our people to develop our country, so that we can continue our efforts to build a cohesive and harmonious nation.
